clinician.final_diagnosis: CNS PTLD, specifically high-grade diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the activated B-cell phenotype.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old liver transplant recipient on immunosuppression presented with acute neurological symptoms including generalized weakness, headaches, confusion, disorientation, papilledema, and focal neurological deficits. Initial CT was negative for hemorrhage. Brain MRI revealed multiple ring-enhancing lesions with vasogenic edema. A brain biopsy showed diffuse infiltrates of atypical CD20-positive B-lymphoid cells, which were pathologically classified as high-grade diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the activated B-cell phenotype.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient is a 64-year-old liver transplant recipient on immunosuppression (mycophenolate and tacrolimus) presenting with neurological symptoms.

Brain MRI revealed multiple ring-enhancing lesions, primarily in the right frontal lobe, temporoparietal regions, and left parietal lobe, with the largest measuring 2.7 cm, associated with moderate vasogenic edema.

Brain biopsy revealed diffuse infiltrates of closely packed intermediate to large mononuclear cells with scant cytoplasm, perivascular infiltrate of atypical lymphoid cells, and widespread infiltrate of neoplastic intermediate to large lymphocytes positive for the B-cell marker CD20.
The pathological classification of the biopsy specimen was high-grade diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the activated B-cell phenotype.
